evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.text: The entry lists one small-seal-script example for 點 and no oracle-bone or bronze examples. It gives the Shuowen explanation 小黑也。从黑，占聲 and analyzes the original sense as a small black mark. The entry’s form inventory establishes what this database records; absence from its inventory does not prove that no earlier witness exists.

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: cited lexical uses and attributed dates
evidence.text: The entry cites 點 in Jin-period 《晉書·文苑傳·袁宏》 in the sense of an unblemished white jade with no spot; it also quotes 《爾雅·釋器》 with Guo Pu’s gloss linking 點 to writing over a character. Further examples are attributed to Wei-period writing for ornamenting, Southern Song 《世說新語》 for textual punctuation, a Song poem for raindrops, and a Tang poem for checking/counting. These separate citations do not by themselves establish a chronological chain of semantic change.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：點

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 占 independent graphic history and lexical use
evidence.text: The 占 entry records oracle-bone forms and explains them as 卜 plus 口, or a related兆 form plus 口, associated with observing divination cracks. It cites oracle-bone examples including 《合集》21068 and 《合集》116反, and separately describes later Warring States forms and uses. This supports 占’s independent history and use; it does not establish an early 點 graph.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：占

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: Middle Chinese readings of 點 and 占
evidence.text: For 點 the entry gives 多忝切 and Middle Chinese categories 端母, 添/忝 rhyme, rising tone, Division IV. For 占 it gives 職廉切 in level tone and 章豔切 in departing tone, with 章母, 鹽 rhyme, Division III. These are distinct Middle Chinese readings/categories, not a same-system Old Chinese reconstruction comparison. The database labels 占 the phonetic component, but the consulted material does not quantify the earlier sound match.

evidence.field: modern readings and proposed Old Chinese comparison
evidence.text: A search result for the 點 entry reports Mandarin diǎn and identifies 黑 as semantic and 占 as phonetic. It supplies Baxter-Sagart-style forms 點 /*tˤemʔ/ and 占 /*tem/, while warning that the modern Mandarin readings differ after historical sound change. The result was inspected as returned by web search; direct page opening timed out, so the original entry and its reconstruction notation were not independently checked in an opened page.

evidence.text: The source explicitly records 點 as 黑 semantic plus 占 phonetic and provides a seal-script witness but no oracle-bone or bronze examples in its listing. The consonant and rhyme categories supplied for 點 and the two readings of 占 differ in Middle Chinese; the available evidence does not settle the compound’s exact early phonological relationship. The traditional component analysis should not be transferred literally to simplified 点, whose present lower 灬 shape is associated graphically with the older character.

gaps: No glyph image is proposed: the relevant Commons category result did not establish an inspectable file description page, exact image URL, and reuse-rights statement for 點-seal.svg. The direct Commons page attempts failed, and the exact Xiaoxuetang 点-specific record could not be loaded.

The inspected CUHK entry provides no securely dated earliest inscriptional 點 witness in its listings; it shows one small-seal example but no oracle-bone or bronze forms. Its database’s absent entries do not prove the character never occurred in those script traditions.
The earliest lexical attestation is not fixed here. The sources cite a Shuowen definition and later-attributed classical examples, but do not supply a complete corpus chronology.

The cited senses include spot, textual marking or erasure, ornamenting, drop, and checking/counting. Their examples are attributed to different works and periods, but the sources do not establish every semantic transition between them.

Although the database explicitly analyzes 占 as 點’s phonetic component, the inspected same-source Middle Chinese categories differ. No independently verified same-system Old Chinese comparison for both relevant readings was obtained, so the historical sound correspondence remains unresolved.

The modern simplified 点 corresponds to traditional 點, but the inspected references do not establish its complete graphic development or a precise adoption date. Do not treat the present 灬 shape as proof that fire was the original semantic component.
No source inspected here supports a whole-graph phonetic loan or borrowing based on the name of a depicted object. The repository’s unrelated fusion note remains uncorroborated.

limitations.text: A Commons search result identified 點-seal.svg in a relevant seal-script component category, but the file description page could not be inspected, so no direct image URL, exact provenance, or asset-specific rights claim is established. Xiaoxuetang is documented as a historical-form database, but its 點-specific query could not be accessed. No glyph image is proposed.
